question:
Solve for $k$ if the system of equations 

$\begin{aligned} x + y + z &= 3 \\ 2x + 3y + 2z &= 6 \\ x + 2y + kz &= 4 \end{aligned}$ 

has infinitely many solutions.
explanation:
For infinitely many solutions, the determinant of coefficients $\Delta$ is zero.
Let
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & k \end{vmatrix}$

Expand along first row:
$= 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 2 & k \end{vmatrix} - 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 1 & k \end{vmatrix} + 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix}$

Calculate minors:
$\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 2 & k \end{vmatrix} = 3k - 4$
$\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 1 & k \end{vmatrix} = 2k - 2$
$\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 4 - 3 = 1$

Substitute:
$= 1(3k-4) - 1(2k - 2) + 1(1)$
$= 3k - 4 - 2k + 2 + 1$
$= (3k - 2k) + (-4+2+1)$
$= k -1$

Set $\Delta = 0$:
$k-1=0 \implies k=1$

Thus, $k=1$ is the required value.
